name: Exposed joinery
summary: A joint that stays in view, so that the way of making is part of the look.
how: Cut the joint in the main wood: a through-tenon of 6 to 12mm shows beyond the face.
Peg the joint with a wooden pin of 8 to 12mm; do not hide it with filler or paint.
Use one joint type in a room or a building; repeat it at each corner.

origin.note: Egyptian carpenters lock the parts of chairs, beds and chests with mortise-and-tenon joints and leave the joints in view.

adoptions.via: Shaker joiners show dovetails and tenons on plain chests and chairs.
Gustav Stickley sells Craftsman furniture with through-tenons that show on the face.
Greene and Greene build the Gamble House in Pasadena with pegged and exposed timber joints.
Peter Zumthor and other critical regionalists keep the joint and the junction as the only ornament.
